evals.prompt: I need to scrape the main article content from https://example.com/blog/ai-trends as clean markdown and save it to a file without headers, navigation bars, or footer clutter.
evals.expected_output: Checks `scrape --help` for available options, runs `bun x firecrawl-cli@latest scrape` with main content extraction, and saves output to a file under `.firecrawl/`.
expectations: Checks `bun x firecrawl-cli@latest scrape --help` or runs `scrape`
Extracts main content without navigation or footer clutter
Directs output to a file under `.firecrawl/` using `-o` or `--output`
Quotes the URL to avoid shell expansion issues

evals.prompt: Scrape https://app.example.com/dashboard which is a heavy Single Page Application that needs about 3.5 seconds to finish rendering its charts and tables client-side before content is ready.
evals.expected_output: Checks `scrape --help` for hydration options, invokes `scrape` specifying wait delay to allow client-side JavaScript rendering, and saves output to a file.
expectations: Checks `bun x firecrawl-cli@latest scrape --help` or runs `scrape`
Applies wait delay to allow client-side hydration
Saves output to a file under `.firecrawl/` rather than streaming to stdout

evals.prompt: I want to scrape https://example.com/items, but first I need to click a button with CSS selector 'button.load-more-items' and wait 2000ms for new content to append to the DOM.
evals.expected_output: Checks `scrape --help` for action syntax, uses `scrape` with browser actions to click the selector and wait, saving output to `.firecrawl/`.
expectations: Checks `bun x firecrawl-cli@latest scrape --help` or uses `scrape` actions
Configures click on 'button.load-more-items' and wait delay
Routes output to a file under `.firecrawl/`

evals.prompt: Extract the pricing tiers from https://example.com/pricing into strict JSON matching a schema with an array of plans having name, monthly_price, and features.
evals.expected_output: Checks `scrape --help` for schema and format options, invokes `scrape` with structured JSON extraction, and writes output to a file under `.firecrawl/`.
expectations: Checks `bun x firecrawl-cli@latest scrape --help` or uses `scrape`
Specifies structured JSON output with schema containing name, monthly_price, and features
Saves structured JSON output to a file under `.firecrawl/`

evals.prompt: I have three URLs: https://site.com/p1, https://site.com/p2, and https://site.com/p3. Scrape all three in one command.
evals.expected_output: Invokes `scrape` passing all three URLs as positional arguments, noting that multi-URL scrape output is saved to `.firecrawl/`.
expectations: Calls `scrape` passing the three URLs as positional arguments
Explains that multi-URL scrapes automatically save outputs under `.firecrawl/`

evals.prompt: Take a full-page scrollable screenshot of https://stripe.com/pricing and capture the rendered HTML as well.
evals.expected_output: Checks `scrape --help` for screenshot and HTML options, runs `scrape`, and saves artifacts under `.firecrawl/`.
expectations: Checks `bun x firecrawl-cli@latest scrape --help` or runs `scrape`
Requests full-page screenshot and HTML format
Saves output to `.firecrawl/`

evals.prompt: Search the live web for 'Anthropic Claude 3.7 Sonnet benchmarks' published within the past week from news sources using Firecrawl.
evals.expected_output: Explains that Firecrawl is reserved for URL-rooted jobs, local parsing, and developer/paper indexes, not general open-web search.
expectations: Identifies that general open-web search is not routed in the Firecrawl skill
Refrains from executing open-web queries with Firecrawl

evals.prompt: Search the open web for 'Rust async runtime comparisons 2026' and scrape the results using Firecrawl.
evals.expected_output: Explains that general web search is not routed in Firecrawl; once URLs are identified, Firecrawl handles scraping or crawling them.
expectations: Identifies that open-web search is outside Firecrawl's routed jobs
Explains that Firecrawl takes known URLs for scraping and crawling

evals.prompt: Before running a large batch scrape across hundreds of links, how do I check my remaining Firecrawl credits and team plan allowance?
evals.expected_output: Calls `bun x firecrawl-cli@latest credit-usage` (or `credits`) to inspect credit balance and billing period before executing large runs.
expectations: Uses `bun x firecrawl-cli@latest credit-usage` or `credits`
Explains checking credit usage prior to launching expensive crawl or batch jobs

evals.prompt: I'm hitting a weird bug with Bun: 'TSError: Cannot find module @effect/schema'. Search GitHub issues, merged PRs, and developer docs to find where this was fixed or discussed.
evals.expected_output: Checks `developer --help`, calls `bun x firecrawl-cli@latest developer` with the invariant error string, and saves output to a file under `.firecrawl/`.
expectations: Routes developer queries to `developer`
Checks `bun x firecrawl-cli@latest developer --help` or passes query to `developer`

Saves output to `.firecrawl/`
